The Virgin Mary. The mother of Jesus, revered in Christian tradition as the Virgin Mary because she conceived Jesus while remaining a virgin. She appears prominently in the birth narratives of Matthew and Luke and is present at key moments in Jesus's ministry and crucifixion, becoming a central figure in Christian devotion and theology. She conceived Jesus through divine intervention while engaged to Joseph, a carpenter. She was visited by the Archangel Gabriel who announced her pregnancy, an event known as the Annunciation. She gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem after traveling from Nazareth during a Roman census. She was present at the wedding at Cana, where Jesus performed his first recorded miracle by turning water into wine. She stood at the foot of Jesus's cross during the Crucifixion, witnessing his death. In Catholic and Orthodox traditions, she ascended to heaven after her earthly life in what is known as the Assumption. She is venerated with prayers, feast days celebrating her birthday on September 8 and the Assumption on August 15, and with artistic depictions across Christian denominations.
